title: A proof of the Bollobás–Nikiforov conjecture in Lean
abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Bollobás–Nikiforov conjecture (2007) and of the matrix theorems that prove it. Let G be a finite simple graph with adjacency eigenvalues lambda_1 >= lambda_2 >= ..., m edges and clique number omega(G). The conjecture states that every noncomplete graph on at least two vertices satisfies lambda_1^2 + lambda_2^2 <= 2 (1 - 1/omega(G)) m. The formalization proves it (BN.lambda1_sq_add_lambda2_sq_le) as a consequence of a weighted spectral inequality: for every symmetric entrywise nonnegative matrix B with zero diagonal supported on the edges of G, the sum F(B) of the squares of the two largest positive eigenvalues of B is at most (1 - 1/omega(G)) ||B||_F^2 (BN.weighted). The weighted inequality rests on a complete-positivity theorem for planar Gram matrices: if z_1, ..., z_n in R^2 lie in a closed half-plane through the origin and X is their Gram matrix, then M(X) = X o X + sum over i < j with X_ij < 0 of X_ij^2 (e_i - e_j)(e_i - e_j)^T is completely positive (BN.matrix_theorem), proved by an ordered elimination, a Schur complement identified as a weighted Laplacian plus a matrix with an explicit three-column nonnegative factorization, and total nonnegativity of two rectangular kernels. A variational argument then removes the half-plane hypothesis from the scalar inequality: for every real positive semidefinite X of rank at most two, sum_{i,j} (A_G)_ij (X_ij)_+^2 <= (1 - 1/omega(G)) ||X||_F^2 (BN.gram_le), which also identifies the rank-two conic parameter chi''_{vec,3}(G) of Coutinho, Spier and Zhang with omega(G) (BN.chiVec3_eq_cliqueNum), settling their Conjectures 2 and 3 without a lower bound on the clique number. Previously the conjecture was known for weakly perfect graphs (Ando–Lin), triangle-free graphs (Lin–Ning–Wu), regular graphs (Zhang), graphs with few triangles (Kumar–Pragada, Zeng–Zhang), asymptotically almost surely for random graphs (Liu–Bu), and with weaker constants for all graphs (Coutinho–Spier–Zhang). All five headline theorems are proved with no sorry and depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
